Cool Hands, Safe Hands

When temperatures climb, thick winter gloves become unbearable, leading some riders to choose inadequate or no gloves. Proper summer gloves provide essential hand protection while allowing airflow to keep your grip secure. In a slide, your hands instinctively reach out to break the fall — making gloves one of the most critical safety items.

What Makes a Good Summer Glove

Summer gloves balance airflow against protection. The best use perforated leather or mesh panels on hand backs where airflow is most effective, while maintaining solid palm protection and knuckle armour.

  • Knuckle protection — Hard or soft armour over knuckles is essential. Carbon fibre, thermoplastic, and viscoelastic options all work.
  • Palm sliders — Reinforced palm with slider prevents hand catching on tarmac during a slide.
  • Finger protection — Reinforced seams and padding across fingers reduce injury risk.
  • Touch-screen compatibility — Operating phone or GPS without removing gloves is a genuine touring convenience.
  • Pre-curved fingers — Reduces hand fatigue by matching the natural grip shape on handlebars.

Best Summer Gloves 2026

Alpinestars SP-8 V3 Air — Premium perforated leather with hard knuckle protector and reinforced palm. Excellent airflow through perforations with top-tier protection.

Rev It Ritmo — Lightweight short-cuff with goat leather palm, mesh back, and TPR knuckle protector. Touchscreen-compatible fingertips.

Held Air Stream 3 — German-made with kangaroo leather palm and SuperFabric knuckle area. Among the best airflow available with superb fit.

Oxford RP-6S — Budget summer glove with carbon knuckle, reinforced palm, and mesh panels. Remarkable protection at the price.

Never ride without gloves, even in a heatwave. Road rash on palms and fingers is excruciating and takes weeks to heal. Summer gloves let the breeze through while keeping your skin intact.

Glove Care

Summer gloves absorb sweat quickly. Hand wash regularly in lukewarm water with mild soap. Never machine wash leather. Air dry naturally away from direct heat. Carry a spare pair in luggage for unexpected showers.

When to Switch to Summer Gloves

Most UK riders switch to summer gloves when daytime temperatures consistently exceed fifteen degrees Celsius, typically from May through September. In the shoulder months of April and October, carry both summer and winter gloves in your luggage and switch depending on conditions. For Scottish and Highland touring, summer gloves may only be appropriate for July and August, with three-season gloves being more practical for the cooler temperatures encountered at altitude and on exposed coastal roads throughout the rest of the touring season in northern Britain.
